top_choice_rationale: Optical lattice clocks (Katori, Ye) are a mature, cleanly attributed two-laureate achievement: the magic-wavelength lattice idea and its realisation took frequency standards to the 1e-18 level, a result confirmed across many laboratories, with a narrow citation scope that matches exactly what was done. The twisted bilayer graphene proposal (P002) is a high-quality prediction-plus-discovery pair, but the unresolved pairing mechanism, the omitted first author of the 2018 experiments under a three-name limit and the disputed credit chain make its allocation and citation harder to defend, so it ranks second. No award is last because at least two fully accepted achievements are available.
recusal_note: none apparent from profile; B007 and B005 have no documented link to Chalmers or WACQT collaborators in the profile
